core.why: An empty write is not queued by the core; the consent panel is not opened to approve copying nothing (the TypeScript policy opens it with an empty text).

libghostty-vt only delivers writes for the standard clipboard; a selection-only target ('s') is dropped by the VT, where the TypeScript policy offers it. Needs a decision (a binding change would be needed to see the target).
A target list that includes the selection ('cs') is not treated as the standard clipboard by libghostty-vt; the TypeScript policy offers it.
An unknown target letter ('x') is taken as the standard clipboard by libghostty-vt and offered for consent; the TypeScript policy rejects it. Still only an offer to the user, never applied.
Repeated targets ('ccc') are not accepted by libghostty-vt; the TypeScript policy accepts any run of c and s.
